intro: Some attention variants replace softmax with a positive feature map. Associativity then lets them combine keys and values before evaluating each query.
task: Implement ELU-plus-one kernel attention with an explicit denominator regularizer. Compare the associative calculation with a small, directly constructed kernel matrix.
requirements: queries has nonempty shape (Q,D), keys is (K,D), and values is (K,V), with K,V>0. Query and key sequence lengths may differ.
Use phi(x)=x+1 when x>0, and phi(x)=exp(x) otherwise. Compute numerator=phi(queries)@(phi(keys).T@values) and denominator=phi(queries)@sum(phi(keys),axis=0).

Return numerator/(denominator[:,None]+1e-6) as a (Q,V) array. The epsilon is added, not used as a lower clamp. This operation is bidirectional kernel attention, not softmax attention or a causal recurrence.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Build a feature-by-value summary
hints.body: phi(keys).T@values has shape (D,V), independent of the query count.

hints.title: Evaluate the feature map by branches
hints.body: Use exp only for nonpositive entries. Computing exp for every entry before selecting can overflow on large positive inputs.

explanation: Without epsilon, the output is a normalized weighted sum with weights given by positive feature inner products. The additive epsilon slightly reduces the total weight, especially when the kernel mass is very small.
The feature map changes the attention rule. Reassociation is algebraically valid for this kernel, but it does not make the result equal to ordinary softmax attention.

Adapted the upstream associative ELU-plus-one attention and its additive 1e-6 denominator. Used direct exp(x) on the negative branch to avoid cancellation and masked branch evaluation to avoid positive exponential overflow.
